<p style="text-align: center;"><span style="font-family: Arvo; font-size: 13px; color: #8a8a95;">Updated September 2026</span></p>
<p>[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="15" screen_mobile_spacer_size="10"][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][vc_column_text css=""]<span style="font-family: Arvo;"><strong>Oddtoe</strong> is an experiential design and generative-AI animation studio based in Melbourne, creating projection, installation, and animated work for events, venues, and galleries. This is a <strong>use case</strong>: how a campaign uses <strong>Oddtoe</strong> to pull off a political stunt, from the first idea to the photograph that gets printed. The example running through it is a set of carried heads. The same steps apply to an inflatable, a projection, a mascot costume, or a kinetic sculpture.</span>[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][vc_column_text css=""]<span style="font-family: Arvo;">The work is designed by a <strong>political cartoonist</strong> &#8212; chief designer for a Washington DC paper, and an editorial cartoonist before that. That background matters here, because a rally photograph and a daily cartoon are the same problem. You get one picture to make the argument, and nobody sticks around for an explanation. The stunts people remember passed that test: the Trump baby blimp over Parliament Square, or the pink boat Extinction Rebellion parked in Oxford Circus.</span>[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer artwork, and the footage afterwards" heading_margin="margin-bottom:10px;"]What Does a Campaign Actually Get?[/dfd_heading][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" artwork it came from, and the photos and video from the day. All of it is yours to keep, crate included, and it goes out again at the next action.</strong></span>

<span style="font-family: Arvo;">&#8226; <strong>The object</strong> &#8212; in this example four oversized heads, cane frame and papier-m&acirc;ch&eacute; skin<br />&#8226; <strong>The character artwork</strong> &#8212; the same designs flat, for placards, posters and social<br />&#8226; <strong>A crate</strong> it packs into and travels in<br />&#8226; <strong>Photos and video</strong> from the day, ready for news editors and for phones</span>[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][vc_column_text css=""]<span style="font-family: Arvo;">People tend to forget about the artwork. The object is built from finished character designs, so the campaign also owns drawings that work on a poster, a placard, a t-shirt and a phone screen without redrawing anything.</span>

<span style="font-family: Arvo;">The object can be whatever the idea needs: carried heads, a <strong><a class="dfd-custom-link-decorated" href="/artist-designer/inflatable-artist/">giant inflatable</a></strong>, a <strong><a class="dfd-custom-link-decorated" href="/artist-designer/mascot-designer/">mascot costume</a></strong>, a <strong><a class="dfd-custom-link-decorated" href="/artist-designer/kinetic-sculptor/">kinetic sculpture</a></strong>, or a <strong><a class="dfd-custom-link-decorated" href="/artist-designer/projection-artist/">projection</a></strong> on a building after dark, with the same characters <strong><a class="dfd-custom-link-decorated" href="/what-is-generative-ai-animation/">animated</a></strong>. They are designed together, so what goes up on the wall is the same character as the one in the street.</span>[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][vc_column_text css=""]<span style="font-family: Arvo;">A political cartoon and a protest photograph do the same job. You get about a second of someone&#8217;s attention, and if the picture needs explaining you have already lost them.</span>

<span style="font-family: Arvo;"><strong>Oddtoe</strong> drew editorial cartoons at college in Delaware, then worked as political cartoonist and chief designer for a Washington DC paper. Years of picking which single image a political story runs with, and watching an editor bin the ones that missed, usually for being too clever.</span>[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][vc_column_text css=""]<span style="font-family: Arvo;">More recently, an illustration and cover design for a US House candidate&#8217;s fundraiser &#8212; a donkey bullying an elephant. Blunt, and it still reads printed small.</span>

<span style="font-family: Arvo;">The same instinct decides what a protest object should be. Out of twelve photographs from twelve actions, a news editor runs one. The job is to be that one.</span>

<span style="font-family: Arvo;">It also decides what to leave out. A head that needs a caption has failed, and so does one that turns into a blob from across a square.</span>[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="40" screen_tablet_spacer_size="30" screen_mobile_spacer_size="30"][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row bg_check="row-background-dark" dfd_enable_overlay="" dfd_row_responsive_enable="dfd-row-responsive-enable" responsive_styles="padding_left_mobile:10|padding_right_mobile:10" anchor="compare"][vc_column][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="60" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="60" screen_tablet_spacer_size="50" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][dfd_heading enable_delimiter="" style="style_02" title_font_options="tag:h2|font_size:90|font_family:BebasNeueRegular|line_height:84|letter_spacing:0" title_responsive="font_size_tablet:66|line_height_tablet:62|font_size_mobile:44|line_height_mobile:42" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3|font_size:40|font_family:QwigleyRegular" subtitle="Where the money actually goes" heading_margin="margin-bottom:10px;"]Placards, a Stage, or Something Built?[/dfd_heading][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/6"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="2/3"][vc_column_text css=""]<span style="font-family: Arvo;">A campaign budget usually has one line for the visible part of an action. This is what that line buys three different ways.</span>

<div style="overflow-x: auto;">
<table style="width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse !important; background-color: #000000 !important; border: none !important;">
<thead>

<tr><td style="padding: 12px 18px; text-align: left; background-color: #000000 !important; border: none !important; border-bottom: 1px solid #3a2f2c !important; color: #ffffff !important;"><strong>What it costs</strong></td><td style="padding: 12px 18px; text-align: left; background-color: #000000 !important; border: none !important; border-bottom: 1px solid #3a2f2c !important; color: #ffffff !important;">Cheap per unit, spent again every action</td><td style="padding: 12px 18px; text-align: left; background-color: #000000 !important; border: none !important; border-bottom: 1px solid #3a2f2c !important; color: #ffffff !important;">A large single-day hire</td><td style="padding: 12px 18px; text-align: left; background-color: #000000 !important; border: none !important; border-bottom: 1px solid #3a2f2c !important; color: #ffffff !important;">One build, spread over years</td></tr>
<tr><td style="padding: 12px 18px; text-align: left; background-color: #140f0e !important; border: none !important; border-bottom: 1px solid #3a2f2c !important; color: #ffffff !important;"><strong>How long it lasts</strong></td><td style="padding: 12px 18px; text-align: left; background-color: #140f0e !important; border: none !important; border-bottom: 1px solid #3a2f2c !important; color: #ffffff !important;">One rally, if it does not rain</td><td style="padding: 12px 18px; text-align: left; background-color: #140f0e !important; border: none !important; border-bottom: 1px solid #3a2f2c !important; color: #ffffff !important;">Gone by Monday morning</td><td style="padding: 12px 18px; text-align: left; background-color: #140f0e !important; border: none !important; border-bottom: 1px solid #3a2f2c !important; color: #ffffff !important;">Years, in a crate between actions</td></tr>
<tr><td style="padding: 12px 18px; text-align: left; background-color: #000000 !important; border: none !important; border-bottom: 1px solid #3a2f2c !important; color: #ffffff !important;"><strong>What a news editor does</strong></td><td style="padding: 12px 18px; text-align: left; background-color: #000000 !important; border: none !important; border-bottom: 1px solid #3a2f2c !important; color: #ffffff !important;">Scrolls past it</td><td style="padding: 12px 18px; text-align: left; background-color: #000000 !important; border: none !important; border-bottom: 1px solid #3a2f2c !important; color: #ffffff !important;">Crops it out of the frame</td><td style="padding: 12px 18px; text-align: left; background-color: #000000 !important; border: none !important; border-bottom: 1px solid #3a2f2c !important; color: #ffffff !important;">Runs it, because nothing else looks like it</td></tr>
<tr><td style="padding: 12px 18px; text-align: left; background-color: #140f0e !important; border: none !important; border-bottom: 1px solid #3a2f2c !important; color: #ffffff !important;"><strong>Who has to operate it</strong></td><td style="padding: 12px 18px; text-align: left; background-color: #140f0e !important; border: none !important; border-bottom: 1px solid #3a2f2c !important; color: #ffffff !important;">Whoever is holding it</td><td style="padding: 12px 18px; text-align: left; background-color: #140f0e !important; border: none !important; border-bottom: 1px solid #3a2f2c !important; color: #ffffff !important;">A crew and a technician</td><td style="padding: 12px 18px; text-align: left; background-color: #140f0e !important; border: none !important; border-bottom: 1px solid #3a2f2c !important; color: #ffffff !important;">A few volunteers</td></tr>
<tr><td style="padding: 12px 18px; text-align: left; background-color: #000000 !important; border: none !important; border-bottom: 1px solid #3a2f2c !important; color: #ffffff !important;"><strong>What you own afterwards</strong></td><td style="padding: 12px 18px; text-align: left; background-color: #000000 !important; border: none !important; border-bottom: 1px solid #3a2f2c !important; color: #ffffff !important;">Nothing</td><td style="padding: 12px 18px; text-align: left; background-color: #000000 !important; border: none !important; border-bottom: 1px solid #3a2f2c !important; color: #ffffff !important;">Nothing</td><td style="padding: 12px 18px; text-align: left; background-color: #000000 !important; border: none !important; border-bottom: 1px solid #3a2f2c !important; color: #ffffff !important;">The object and the character artwork</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</div>[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/6"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="60" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="60" screen_tablet_spacer_size="40" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row bg_check="row-background-dark" dfd_enable_overlay="" dfd_row_config="default_row_small_paddings" anchor="who" dfd_row_responsive_enable="dfd-row-responsive-enable" responsive_styles="padding_left_mobile:10|padding_right_mobile:10"][vc_column][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="60" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="60" screen_tablet_spacer_size="50" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][dfd_heading enable_delimiter="" style="style_02" title_font_options="tag:h2|font_size:90|font_family:BebasNeueRegular|line_height:84|letter_spacing:0" title_responsive="font_size_tablet:66|line_height_tablet:62|font_size_mobile:44|line_height_mobile:42" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3|font_size:40|font_family:QwigleyRegular" subtitle="Campaigns, unions, and NGOs" heading_margin="margin-bottom:10px;"]Who Commissions Work Like This?[/dfd_heading][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][vc_column_text css=""]<span style="font-family: Arvo;">Non-profits and NGOs, grassroots campaigns, unions, advocacy organisations, and political campaigns. What they all have is a date in the diary and something they need people to see.</span>

<span style="font-family: Arvo;"><strong>Campaigns with a fixed date</strong> &#8212; a launch, a vote, a summit &#8212; need one day to produce a month of coverage.</span>

<span style="font-family: Arvo;"><strong>Unions</strong> want objects that come out again and again, because the same members turn up several times a year.</span>[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][vc_column_text css=""]<span style="font-family: Arvo;"><strong>NGOs and advocacy organisations</strong> need artwork that still works when volunteers in three cities are running it and there is no designer in the room. That means artwork files anyone can pick up.</span>

<span style="font-family: Arvo;"><strong>Political campaigns</strong> buy artwork and objects the way they buy everything else. <strong>Oddtoe</strong> has done fundraiser illustration for a US House candidate.</span>

<span style="font-family: Arvo;">Agencies working for any of the above are welcome too: see <strong><a class="dfd-custom-link-decorated" href="/experiential-marketing/">experiential marketing</a></strong>.</span>[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" political groups, and the staffers who run a member&#8217;s diary. <strong>PR agencies</strong> as well &#8212; plenty of this work arrives through a press team rather than the campaign itself.</span>

<span style="font-family: Arvo;">If you already have someone on press, I work to them. They know the outlets and the timing. I build the thing that gives them a picture worth sending, and the two get planned together from the first week.</span>[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][vc_column_text css=""]<span style="font-family: Arvo;"><strong><a class="dfd-custom-link-decorated" href="/artist-designer/street-artist-muralist/">Street art</a></strong> is punk rock for visual artists. You do not need a gallery or a commission or anyone&#8217;s permission, and it gets seen by people who never decided to look at art that day.</span>

<span style="font-family: Arvo;">That is most of why this subject grabs me. A head carried down a street is doing the same job as a paste-up on a wall at four in the morning &#8212; putting the argument where people actually are.</span>[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][vc_column_text css=""]<span style="font-family: Arvo;">I make my own work as well as client work, and sculpture street art is where I want to take that next. So when a protest brief comes in, it is about the closest thing to what I would be making anyway.</span>

<span style="font-family: Arvo;">The practical upside for a campaign is that the person designing the object has a stake in whether it works. I want the photograph to be good for the same reason you do.</span>[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][dfd_spacer <p style="text-align: center;"><span style="font-family: Qwigley; font-size: 36pt;">Questions about</span></p>
<p style="text-align: center;"><span style="font-family: 'Bebas Neue'; font-size: 36pt;">Protest work?</span></p>
[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="30" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][dfd_accordion style="style-3" active_section="1" font_size="18" tab_title_google_fonts="yes" tab_title_custom_fonts="font_family:Arvo%3Aregular%2Citalic%2C700%2C700italic|font_style:700%20bold%20regular%3A700%3Anormal" icon_size="14"][vc_tta_section title="What is this use case, exactly?" tab_id="1757300000001-usecase-protest-faq-1"][vc_column_text css=""]
<p style="text-align: center;">A worked example. It follows one brief - a campaign with a press day and no picture - from the first question through design, fabrication, the day itself, and what the campaign still owns afterwards. It uses carried heads as the example, and an inflatable, a projection, a mascot costume or a kinetic sculpture would follow the same shape.</p>
[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="How long does it take?" tab_id="1757300000002-usecase-protest-faq-2"][vc_column_text css=""]
<p style="text-align: center;">Six to eight weeks from brief to press day for a set of carried heads. Design and approval take the first fortnight, fabrication the next three weeks, and the rest is packing and freight. An inflatable or a mascot costume takes longer, because a specialist maker builds it from the pattern set. A rush is possible but it comes out of the design stage, which is the part worth protecting.</p>
[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="Can it be shipped outside Australia?" tab_id="1757300000003-usecase-protest-faq-3"][vc_column_text css=""]
<p style="text-align: center;">Yes. Everything is built to crate, and freight and paperwork are handled from this end. Cane and paper are plant material, so treatment and certification are part of the job from the start.</p>
[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="What does it cost?" tab_id="1757300000004-usecase-protest-faq-4"][vc_column_text css=""]
<p style="text-align: center;"><strong>Oddtoe</strong> does not publish prices. Cost is driven by what the object is, how many, how large, how much structure each one needs, and where it has to travel. It is costed the same way as any other <strong><a class="dfd-custom-link-decorated" href="/prop-fabrication-services/">prop fabrication</a></strong> job. Send the brief and the date and you get a quote.</p>
[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="Do we need council permits?" tab_id="1757300000005-usecase-protest-faq-5"][vc_column_text css=""]
<p style="text-align: center;">Usually not for the objects themselves - they are carried, not installed, with no power and no rigging. The permit conversation is about the assembly or the march, which the campaign is already having.</p>
[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="Can we use it more than once?" tab_id="1757300000006-usecase-protest-faq-6"][vc_column_text css=""]
<p style="text-align: center;">That is the point. It goes back in the crate and comes out at the next action. An object built for one press day has usually paid for itself by its third outing.</p>
[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="Can you do the animation and projection as well?" tab_id="1757300000007-usecase-protest-faq-7"][vc_column_text css=""]
<p style="text-align: center;">Yes, and they are designed together when the brief calls for it - the same characters animated and projected after dark. See <strong><a class="dfd-custom-link-decorated" href="/artist-designer/projection-artist/">projection art</a></strong> and <strong><a class="dfd-custom-link-decorated" href="/what-is-generative-ai-animation/">generative AI animation</a></strong>.</p>
[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="Where is Oddtoe based?" tab_id="1757300000008-usecase-protest-faq-8"][vc_column_text css=""]
<p style="text-align: center;"><strong>Oddtoe</strong> is based in Melbourne, Australia. Supplier and business contacts run through Berlin and Los Angeles, and those are the starting points for work in Europe and the United States.</p>
[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][/dfd_accordion][vc_raw_html][/vc_raw_html][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="30" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][dfd_button button_text="Contact Oddtoe" buttom_link_src="url:https%3A%2F%2Fwww.oddtoe.com%2Fcontact-oddtoe%2F|title:Contact%20Oddtoe" style="style_6" background="#8a8f6a" hover_background="#4e5041" border="border-style:none;|border-radius:5px;" hover_border="border-style:none;|border-radius:5px;"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="110" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="90" screen_tablet_spacer_size="60" screen_mobile_spacer_size="60"][/vc_column][vc_column width="1/4"][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row bg_check="row-background-dark" dfd_enable_overlay="" one_page_title="More" anchor="more"][vc_column][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="100" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="90" screen_tablet_spacer_size="80" screen_mobile_spacer_size="80"][vc_column_text css="" item_animation="transition.fadeIn"]
<p style="text-align: center;"><span style="font-family: Qwigley; font-size: 36pt;">Interested in seeing more&#8230; </span></p>
